Nina (arch): Quick sync — thinking about a 'control-plane federation' option for multi-region. Instead of a single global control plane, we delegate policy decisions to a per-region policy engine that syncs a compact decision log. Thoughts?
Mike (infra): Sounds promising. Do you mean each region runs its own 'mini-control-plane' and we replicate decisions async?
Nina (arch): Exactly. Replicate a small ordered log (policy deltas, model pins, tenant consent flags). Strong consensus only for write-critical ops (lease grants). Everything else eventual.
Sara (runtime): One thing to watch: runtime routing needs a clear contract. If a region's policy says "prefer local" but another overrides model version, how does the dataplane resolve? We should define precedence: local policy > customer pin > global override.
Josh (privacy): Important: any replication must honor data residency. For EU tenants the decision log MAY contain only opaque ids and hashes. No PII or tenant data can be shipped outside region. Also need a consent flag checked before any cross-region fallback.
Eli (prodops): For rollout let's define an experiment: 1) federation read-only (policy shadowing), 2) delegate reads to local CP, 3) delegate writes with lease guard. Monitor these metrics: handshake latency, decision divergence, fallback rate.
Sara (runtime): Agreed. Suggest adding a small header the proxy can use: ``X-Region-Policy-Token: <sha256>``, plus ``X-Region-Preference: local|regional|global``. Runtime will treat token mismatch as a signal to consult SLO fallback.
Mike (infra): Implementation detail: we can reuse existing lease service for write-critical operations. Lease token format proposal: ``lease_v1:{region}:{expiry}:{sig}``. Keep validation cheap.
Josh (privacy): Also need a deterministic way to refuse cross-region fallback for restricted tenants. Maybe a tenant flag: ``tenant_geo_policy: eu-only`` that the control plane replicates as an allowlist only (no sensitive payload).
Nina (arch): Good call. Let's keep per-tenant geo_policy as a small enum: [global, prefer_local, region_only:<region_code>]. Replicated as compact events; operators can purge old events.
Eli (prodops): Can we sketch SLOs? I propose: control-plane decision availability (p95 handshake) < 50ms intra-region, < 200ms cross-region; fallback success rate > 99.5 during normal load.
Mike (infra): Those seem reasonable but cross-region 200ms will be tight if we do consensus. That's why I prefer local-first + background sync. For lease issuance we can have a fast primary lease holder per shard and async shadowing.
Sara (runtime): For runtime recovery we should define states: ACTIVE_LOCAL, DELEGATED_REMOTE, READ_ONLY_FAILOVER. Include short log lines so operator tooling can show current state. e.g. ``[region-eu] state=DELEGATED_REMOTE lease=lease_v1:eu:...``
Josh (privacy): Add audit events whenever a decision causes a cross-region route for a tenant that is not 'global'. Critical for compliance.
Nina (arch): Action items: 1) Mike + Sara to prototype proxy header + lease token format (week 1). 2) Josh to draft residency-safe replication rules (week 1). 3) Eli to prepare canary metrics and alert thresholds (week 2). 4) I'll write a short RFC for the federation model (due EOD Fri). Anyone else?
Eli (prodops): I'll add the canary dashboard template and include a synthetic that flips region tokens to simulate mismatch.
deploy-bot: test-deploy: federation-probe-service v0.1 deployed to staging :rocket:
Mike (infra): small note — we should also document operator rollback steps if decision divergence persists (force-consensus mode). Add an operator command: ``redwoodctl cp force-consensus --shard S``.
Sara (runtime): +1. Also add a runtime toggle: ``runtime.feature.controlplane_federation = on|off|shadow`` so we can shadow mode without changing traffic.
Nina (arch): Great. If no blockers I'll spin up the RFC draft now and tag everyone. :white_check_mark:
Josh (privacy): Thanks — I may ping legal for quick signoff on replication primitives once the draft lands.
Nina (arch): will do. Thanks all.
